name: constant-half4-black
rationale: The fragment ignores its position and viewport-index inputs and returns literal half4 (0,0,0,1); one full-coverage fragment replaces the poisoned pixel.

name: linked-single-fft-temp-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded FFT work item with unit extents and strides. The destination-temp path confines writes to the authored output allocation. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert.

name: tile-cell-below-the-alpha-floor-is-cleared-not-tone-mapped
rationale:
No authored case reached `llvm.memset.p4.i64`, which 9 corpus sources name. All nine are the same `vst::splat::hw_rasterizer::resolveTileMemoryKernel` family and this 213-line member is the smallest. Unlike the padding memset in the sibling `llvm.memset.p3.i64` case, THIS one is fully observable: `addrspace(4)` is the imageblock, the call zeroes all sixteen bytes of one tile cell, and the cell is then resolved into a texture where the case can read it.

Each of the 256 threads takes its own cell with `air.imageblock_data(pid, 0, 0)` and reads the half4 there. If the alpha is below 0x1C04 -- 0.003921508789375, the coverage floor -- and the `resolveDepth` flag at struct offset 46 is set, the cell is memset to zero; otherwise the thread un-premultiplies, runs the piecewise transfer, applies the `colorCorrection` half3x3, re-premultiplies, and stores the result back with the original alpha. After the barrier, the one thread whose `lid` is 0 checks `gid` against the `min`/`max` bounds and, because `layered` at offset 47 is zero, resolves the whole 16x16 slice into the plain `texture2d` at struct offset 72 with a destination origin of `gid - min`, which the authored bounds make (0, 0).

The tile is deliberately split. The 64 cells where (x + y) is a multiple of four start as (0.5, 0.25, 0.125) with alpha 2^-10, the only alpha under the floor, so each is cleared and resolves to four zero halves; the diagonal stripe they form is a pattern a cell mapping cannot produce by accident. The other 192 carry rgb zero and an alpha of n/16 for n cycling 1 through 15, and take the tone-map arm instead: zero divided by a finite alpha is zero, zero is below the 0x292D transfer knee so the linear arm is selected, the identity `colorCorrection` leaves it zero, and re-multiplying by alpha leaves it zero -- so each resolves to (0, 0, 0, alpha) exactly, with no rounding anywhere. The fifteen-long alpha cycle against a sixteen-wide tile means every column carries a different alpha in every row, so a transposed, shifted or row-strided cell mapping moves at least one texel.

That is the whole counterfactual. A dropped `llvm.memset.p4.i64` leaves all 64 selected cells holding their original (0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 2^-10) -- four different halves in every texel the case is about, and the only texels whose alpha would then be neither 0 nor a multiple of 1/16. A memset that zeroed the right cell but only its first eight bytes would still pass here, and the case does not claim otherwise; what it pins is that the cells the alpha test selected are the cells that get cleared, and that the 192 cells the test did NOT select keep their alpha through the tone-map arm.

The imageblock is 16 by 16 and the threadgroup is 16 by 16, which is the only shape Metal accepts for an aliased implicit imageblock, and the two `full_single_sample` render targets are what put the authored halves into the tile before the kernel runs. The resolve destination starts as 0x5A poison in all 256 texels, so a resolve that wrote the wrong region, or wrote nothing, is visible rather than silently agreeing with a zero background. The other five destinations in the argument buffer are declared because reflection declares them and are never written on this path. Metal refuses a tile smaller than its minimum -- a 2 by 2 imageblock is rejected at render-pass validation with "Invalid tile dimensions" -- which is why the tile is 16 by 16 and not the smallest shape that would separate the branch. This case also stands as the regression guard for the Metal oracle change it forced. Before that change the oracle never made an argument-buffer resource resident on the tile encoder, so Metal dropped this dispatch whole: all four resolve destinations and both render targets read back their authored initial bytes, and the run was still recorded `qualified`. Our own candidate computed the derived answer throughout, so the disagreement was entirely on the oracle side -- the shape that catches it is a tile function reaching a texture through an argument buffer, and no other case in the corpus has it.

name: mix-at-factor-one-answers-y-through-absorbing-magnitudes
rationale: The one in-bounds invocation blends src1 and src2 at an authored factor of exactly 1.0, the point where the two published readings of a linear blend stop agreeing: Metal Shading Language documents mix as x + (y - x) * a, while GLSL.std.450 FMix -- what this translator emits for air.mix -- is x * (1 - a) + y * a. Components 0 and 2 make that difference visible by using magnitudes (1e10, -1e10) that absorb their partner entirely, so y - x rounds to exactly -x and the documented Metal expression would collapse to 0 while the weighted sum returns y. Components 1 and 3 use small magnitudes where both readings agree and act as controls that the invocation ran. Metal answers (1, 7, 3, 5): at a factor of one the hardware returns y exactly on all four components, so the intrinsic evaluates the weighted sum and FMix is the lowering that matches it. The observation depends on no rounding beyond that single absorbing subtraction, which it is designed to expose rather than avoid.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twelve-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 12 and receives exact float4 zero from all eleven linked _uber_clear bodies. A fourteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: reset-specular-indirect-count
rationale: The loop-free entry ignores its grid index and unconditionally replaces the complete poisoned four-byte indirect-specular entry counter with aligned i32 zero.

name: reverse-four-argb8-pixels-through-a-permutation-matrix
rationale: unpack.unorm4x8 and pack.unorm4x8 round-trip a byte exactly, so the case stays byte-authorable as long as nothing between them leaves the b/255 grid. A permutation matrix does not: every dot product is one lane of the input, so the four output pixels are the four input pixels with their channels reversed and no rounding enters. The source row stride is 12 over a 2-pixel row and the destination stride is 8, so the two stride fields cannot be confused for each other, and the four decoy bytes at the end of each source row are never read. Both bias flags are off and both bias vectors hold 9.0, which would saturate every channel if either were applied.

name: saturate-four-argb8-pixels-with-a-unit-post-bias
rationale: The same permutation blit with the post-bias flag on and the post-bias vector set to 1.0, which pushes every channel to at least 1.0 before packing. pack.unorm4x8 clamps to [0,1], so every output byte must be 255; without the clamp the conversion would wrap. Paired with the unbiased case it also pins that the flag byte at offset 105 is the one that selects the post-bias, since the two manifests differ only in that byte and in the post-bias vector.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-nine-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 29 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-eight linked _uber_clear bodies. A thirty-one-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: vertex-id-fullscreen-position-viewport-zero
rationale: Vertex IDs 0, 1, and 2 generate the oversized full-screen triangle (-1,1), (3,1), and (-1,-3), each with z=w=1. The single instance structurally emits viewport zero; the typed position observer records all four covered pixels without authored vertex inputs.

name: linked-single-unit-reduce-multiple-passes-axes-all
rationale: One invocation reduces one float element along axis zero. Every four-lane reduction extent, per-thread count, per-threadgroup count, source and destination bound, broadcast extent, and NDArray size and stride is one, so all loops are bounded by the single authored element.

name: half-twiddle-at-the-zero-angle-is-the-identity-rotation
rationale: One invocation at grid origin. `precision` selects the half branch, so the twiddle angle is `sign * -2*pi * gid.y * gid.x / (float)(half)(threadsPerGrid.x * threadsPerGrid.y)`, and with gid = (0,0,0) both `gid.y` and `gid.x` are zero: the numerator is an exact zero times a finite float, the divisor is (half)1 = 1, and the angle truncates to half zero. `air.cos.f16(0)` must be exactly 1.0h and `air.sin.f16(0)` exactly 0.0h -- every polynomial sin is odd (x times a series) and every polynomial cos carries an x^2 in each term past the leading 1 -- so the complex rotation is the identity and the two seeded halves must come back unchanged. `batchStride` is zero and gid.z is zero, so the pair addressed is element 0 and 1. What this pins: cos and sin of half zero exactly, and the real/imaginary wiring -- the two seeds are 1.5 and -2.25, so a rotation that crossed the real and imaginary terms would swap them. The twelve poisoned bytes after the pair are captured with them. It pins no transcendental value away from zero; at any other angle a half sin/cos is 1-ULP territory on MoltenVK's runtime compiler and is not byte-authorable.

name: half-twiddle-quarter-turn-lands-on-exactly-negative-one
rationale: Four invocations over a 2x2 grid, and only one of them rotates. The twiddle angle is `sign * -2*pi * gid.y * gid.x / (float)(half)(threadsPerGrid.x*threadsPerGrid.y)`, so the three threads with a zero in either grid coordinate see angle zero and leave their pairs alone; thread (1,1) sees -2*pi/4, which truncates to the half -1.5703125 (0xBE48). There sin is -0.99999988, correctly rounded to exactly -1.0h, and cos is 0.00048383. The pair at that thread is seeded (1.0, 2.0) so the cos term cannot survive half rounding: the real output is 1*cos + 2 = 2.000484, which rounds to exactly 2.0, and the imaginary output is 2*cos - 1 = -0.99903235, which rounds to exactly -0.9990234 (0xBBFE). Perturbing cos by three ULP either way leaves both bytes unchanged, so what this pins about cos is only its magnitude; what it pins EXACTLY is sin, where one ULP moves both outputs (sin = -0.99951 gives 0x3FFF/0xBBFD, sin = -1.00098 gives 0x4001/0xBC00). Predicted with a numpy float16 model, then confirmed: Metal and MoltenVK both return 003e80c0004200b8003400c40040febb.

name: three-packed-pixel-formats-at-exact-points
rationale:
One invocation unpacking all three packed pixel formats the corpus uses and no authored case reached: rgb10a2 (40 sources), rg11b10f (35) and rgb9e5 (35). The two shared-exponent formats have no unpack_* spelling in metal_pack; the front end only emits them through the metal_pixel types, so the host is a buffer of rg11b10f<float3> and one of rgb9e5<float3>, read as float3.

Every point is chosen so the answer does not depend on how either back end spells the arithmetic. The rgb10a2 fields are 1023, 341, 512 and alpha 2: dividing each by its 1023 or 3 and multiplying by the reciprocal of that divisor agree bit-for-bit at all four (they are outside the 24 of 1024 numerators where the two forms disagree), and the four values are all distinct, so a swapped or mis-shifted field moves the result. The rg11b10f fields are exponent 15 mantissa 0 (1.0), exponent 16 mantissa 32 (3.0) and, in the 10-bit blue field, exponent 13 mantissa 8 (0.3125); all three exponents are normal, so no half denormal is involved and the widening into a half is lossless. The rgb9e5 word is shared exponent 20 with mantissas 256, 64 and 1, giving 16, 4 and 0.0625 -- three powers of two four decades apart, so an off-by-one in the exponent bias or an implicit leading one moves each of them by at least a factor of two.

name: sampled-half-red-to-float4
rationale: The loop-free fragment samples a uniform one-pixel RGBA16Float texture through its declared static sampler, widens the exact red half value 1 to float, and writes (1, 1, 1, 1) to the RGBA32Float target independent of interpolated coordinates.

name: linked-single-unit-decoupled-lookback-scan-min
rationale: One one-thread threadgroup processes one scan element. scanElements, elementsPerThread, threadgroups, both outer-axis lengths, all temporary-array extents, and every NDArray size and stride are one, bounding each lookback and element loop to the single dispatched lane.

name: constant-half-zero
rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns scalar half zero at color location zero; one full-coverage fragment must replace the exact poisoned R16Float pixel.

name: linked-zero-destination-local-convolution
rationale: The authored destination extent is zero in every dimension. The sole invocation fails the entry bounds check before division, loop construction, source access, destination access, or any linked-function call, leaving the bounded poisoned output unchanged.
